newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Investmentbank Austria top trader barred in Vienna.
newsitem.headline: Investmentbank Austria top trader barred in Vienna.

text.p: The chief trader at Investmentbank Austria, part of the Bank Austria group, has been barred from Vienna trade for his involvement in a late sell-off on October 16, the stock exchange said on Friday.
The bourse said Anton Imre had acted in a way that damaged the Vienna market's image although he had not broken any law.
"Traders must recognise the consequences of their actions," Bank Austria chief executive and Vienna bourse president Gerhard Randa said in the statement.
The stock exchange said Imre had been relieved of his responsibilities and had returned his membership card.
The move was in response to a steep drop in the ATX index in the last five minutes of trade on October 16.
Traders said concerted selling by Bank Austria succeeded in knocking the blue-chip index down to 1,073.54 points from 1,089 just prior to the close.
Earlier on Friday the stock exchange announced plans to introduce a weighted closing price for the ATX and raise the minimum trading volume for market makers.
"We plan to calculate and publish a weighted average for each continuously traded share. Investors can use it as a basis for their portfolios and positions," the bourse said.
"At the same time the minimum trading volume for market makers will be increased. In the next few days we will seek the agreement of market makers," it continued.
Traders forecast the minimum trading volume would rise to 1,000 lots from 500 at present.
They traced Wednesday's 1.38 percent decline in the ATX to a battle between Bank Austria and a second domestic bank.
"One was trying to buy the market up and the other was trying to sell it down," a trader said.
Selling pressure centred on ATX heavyweights oil group OMV, insurer EA-Generali and steel firm VA Stahl, traders said.
EA-Generali ended 5.6 percent down on October 16, VA Stahl 5.5 percent down and OMV four percent down.
